answer: Each identity must hold one commercial fishing quota, auctioned once a year and non-transferable for twelve months. The quota names one vessel, and its catch logs must match the lotus-tagged landing records; a quota with no real landings is suspended. A newcomer waits for the auction, pays about 800 units, then must actually fish to earn weight. One hundred fakes need one hundred quotas: about 80,000 units and a year of waiting. The river of auction records is public, so a bought quota still shows its previous owner, and a velvet-gloved paper quota with no catch history is struck off.
